segments.t: Max has heard that Vika loves him, and he goes straight to his best friend Kostya. The two of them talk it through behind the bar. Max isn't sure whether to be happy or frightened. Listen for the names and the numbers.
Если она меня любит, нужны отношения.
Она не будет терпеть твои глупости.
Вот именно, она начнет меня воспитывать.

'Kostya, it seems Vika loves me!' We hear 'it seems' is one word, the same as in We hear 'it seems to you'. We hear 'loves me' is literally "me loves", with the pointing word before the action word, which is common.
'Great! Or is it?' When they say 'great' is slang. When they say 'or no?' is all Kostya says to cast a doubt. He knows his friend well enough to know where this goes.

'Damn, Kostya, this is a dangerous situation.' Notice the part 'damn' is literally a pancake, and it is what they say instead of a ruder word, much like "darn". Notice the part 'situation' has a local ending. Notice the part 'dangerous' is an descriptive word.
Если она меня любит, нужны отношения.

'If she loves me, a relationship is needed.' In Russian, 'needed' translates uses a multiple ending given In Russian, 'relationship' translates is a multiple word here, "relations". Max thinks like a man doing sums.

'And what is bad about a relationship?' Here, 'what of bad' shows has the same ending as Here, 'nothing terrible' shows. Here, 'in a relationship' shows is literally "in relations". It is Kostya's simple question, the one a good friend asks.

'Then a wedding, and then kids!' The way to express 'and then' is used here. The word for a wedding is used, and the word for children is the same word Vika used at the end of the banquet day. Max counts it off like a list of disasters.
'Why do I need all of this right now?' 'what for to me' is used here is native speech for "why do I need". 'all this' is used here is two words. He sounds like a man who doesn't want to grow up.

'You are simply afraid of adult life.' The action Listen to how 'you are afraid' ends in a self-directed ending bit, and what you fear takes the "of" ending: Listen to how 'life' changes its ending. Listen to how 'adult' is an descriptive word.

'I love freedom and adventures!' The action The speaker uses 'I love' is from the same family as The speaker uses 'favourite'. The speaker uses 'freedom' changes its ending because it is the thing he loves. A girlfriend is not on his list.

'Vika is a mature and smart girl.' There is no "is" here, just the name and the description. Both descriptive words end in a she-word ending bit to agree with a woman, and inside They express 'smart' by sits the root for "mind". Kostya sticks up for Vika.
Она не будет терпеть твои глупости.

'She will not tolerate your nonsense.' The action We hear 'to tolerate' is in the same family as We hear 'patience'. We hear 'nonsense' is literally "foolishnesses", from the descriptive We hear 'foolish'. We hear 'will not' is two words.
Вот именно, она начнет меня воспитывать.

'Exactly, she will start educating me.' When they say 'exactly' is literally "there you are" plus "precisely". The action When they say 'educating' covers bringing up a child, so Max feels she will treat him as a boy.

'Then talk to her honestly.' The adverb for "honestly" grows from the descriptive Notice the part 'honest'. The action Notice the part 'talk' has a starting bit meaning for a while. Notice the part 'with her' is two words.

'No, better that I keep quiet.' The action In Russian, 'to keep quiet' translates is the chunk Barinov barked at the kitchen. In Russian, 'I will keep quiet' translates uses the future time frame auxiliary. His plan is to say nothing, and it will not work. The full thing, one more time.
Если она меня любит, нужны отношения.
Она не будет терпеть твои глупости.
Вот именно, она начнет меня воспитывать.
Kostya tells him to speak to Vika honestly. Max decides to keep quiet, which is the worst plan on offer. Until the next one.

Потом свадьба, а потом что, дети?
